messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Is there a way to get access to my usage metrics
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Is there a way to get access to my usage metrics
messages.body_plain:
On Wed, Mar 2, 2016 at 12:34 PM, Andrew Clark <scott.r...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Andy
>
> That function works fine
> showUsage(appDir = getwd(), appName = NULL, account = NULL,
>   server = NULL, usageType = "hours", from = NULL, until = NULL,
>   interval = NULL)
>
> Couple of points
>  a) Is there a list of usageType and relative time delta options

We only have 'hours' right now. We don't track other account usage types as this time.

We have the following relative time delta's defined (as seconds):

{"s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600, "d": 86400, "w": 604800}

>
> b) If I use the NULL value for from, I get 2 values for most hours (one of them being zero) and the data goes back just a month
> . If I enter a value e.g. from=1446938000, the data goes back further but an hours return is just shown once a day 16:00:00

You can use the interval parameter to change the aggregation window. For example if you want to look at one month of metrics by hour you would use interval="1h". If the interval parameter is not specified it attempts to guess a reasonable default to reduce data points returned.

>
> c) Just to clarify, the time returned is for when the app is being used (or at least is not inactive) by at least one person. It could be more but this data is not available, right?

Actually if you upgrade to the latest version of rsconnect from GitHub, I just added a new 'showMetrics' function last week. It works similarly as showUsage, and is also poorly documented:

# from your application directory
metrics.connections <- showMetrics("container.shiny.connections", "shiny.connections.active")
metrics.cpu <- showMetrics("container.cpu", c("cpu.user", "cpu.system"))
metrics.mem <- showMetrics("container.memory", c("memory.total_rss", "memory.total_cache"))
>

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Use gurobi with Shinyapps.io ?
messages.body_plain:
Gurobi is an R package distributed with the commercial Gurobi software package.

Unless shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> has licensing to use Gurobi--which I doubt--then you won't be able to do this.

Your options are:

a) use shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> with a free solver, eg. lpsolve using the lpSolveAPI package. But this will take longer to solve things than Gurobi.

b) host apps on your own server with Gurobi configured. But I am not sure what the licensing is like for Gurobi and if this is allowed.

c) a combination of the two. Host your app on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> have it send problems to your server for processing, and then send the results back to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. Again, similar concerns with licensing apply.

Cheers,

Jeff

messages.subject: Incomplete googleVis motion chart in rMarkdown using Shiny
messages.subject_clean: Incomplete googleVis motion chart in rMarkdown using Shiny
messages.body_plain:
up vote0down votefavorite <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/35898624/incomplete-googlevis-motion-chart-in-rmarkdown-using-shiny#>

I'm trying to make an interactive rMarkdown with a googleVis motion chart in it. The idea is to get a report where I can filter my data and then get a motion chart. So, right now I've got everything working right except that when I run my Document the motion chart is incomplete. Inspecting the html code I found that this is because of the iframe height I know that I can change these direct form the html code but I need a way to change it directly from the Shiny code but I've not been able to find the way. Can anyone please help me?

Here is an example of what I'm trying to do but using the WorldBank dataset:

```{r,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}
#Load Packages

    library(shiny)
    library(rmarkdown)
    library(googleVis)
    library(WDI)
    library(dplyr)

    #Get data
    inds <- c('SP.DYN.TFRT.IN <http://SP.DYN.TFRT.IN>','SP.DYN.LE00.IN <http://SP.DYN.LE00.IN>', 'SP.POP.TOTL',
              'NY.GDP.PCAP.CD <http://NY.GDP.PCAP.CD>', 'SE.ADT.1524.LT.FE.ZS')
    indnams <- c("fertility.rate", "life.expectancy", "population",
                 "GDP.per.capita.Current.USD", "15.to.25.yr.female.literacy")
    wdiData <- WDI(country="all", indicator=inds,
                   start=1960, end=format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"), extra=TRUE)
    colnum <- match(inds, names(wdiData))

    names(wdiData)[colnum] <- indnams
    ## Create a motion chart
    WorldBank <- droplevels(subset(wdiData, !region %in% "Aggregates")) %>%
      mutate(latlon = paste(latitude,longitude,sep=":"))

    WorldBank <- readRDS("WorldBank_Data.RDS") %>%
      mutate(region=as.character(region))
    #Filter function
    filter_and_graph <- function(rgn){
      graph_data <- WorldBank %>%
        filter(region == rgn)

      M <- gvisMotionChart(graph_data,
                         idvar="country", timevar="year",
                         xvar="life.expectancy", yvar="fertility.rate",
                         colorvar="population", sizevar="population",
                         options=list(width=800, height=600))
      return(M)
    }

    #Shiny in markdown
    shinyApp(
      ui = fluidPage(selectInput("rgn",
                  "Choose your region",
                  choices = unique(WorldBank$region),
                  selected = "Sub-Saharan Africa (all income levels)"),
        htmlOutput("graph")

      ),
      server = function(input, output){
        output$graph <- renderGvis({filter_and_graph(input$rgn)})
      }
    )

```

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] General Shinyapp server query
messages.body_plain:
We do not offer any CDN services with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. That does not preclude you from using your own CDN, if you are comfortable with setting it up and managing it.

As for reverse proxying, shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> does use proxying, and allows an application be backed by multiple instances if you are in a paid plan. I'm not sure why you would want your own reverse proxy in front of shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Message ERROR that stop the App - HELP
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Message ERROR that stop the App - HELP
messages.body_plain:
Shiny apps that are deployed on a server are not compatible with tcltk.  Shiny is presuming that the UI is an html UI.  Tcltk starts up its own UI.  When you run an app with tcltk locally it works because it has access to the underlying graphics display and can start the UI.  When you run such an app on the server, the application doesn't have access to the UI.

I don't know enough about the packages you are using but you might be able to get the UI you need by using Shiny instead of relying on the package with a custom tcltk UI.

packrat doesn't support R-Forge without additional configuration, so if you uninstall and re-install the packages from CRAN instead it should just work.

options(repos = c("R-Forge" = "https://R-Forge.R-project.org <https://r-forge.r-project.org/>", CRAN="https://cran.rstudio.com"))

To: bme....@gmail.com; shinyap...@googlegroups.com

Hi Ben,

packrat doesn't support R-Forge without additional configuration, so if you uninstall and re-install the packages from CRAN instead it should just work.
It is possible that doing something like:

options(repos = c("R-Forge" = "https://R-Forge.R-project.org <https://r-forge.r-project.org/>", CRAN="https://cran.rstudio.com"))

will work, but that is untested and YMMV.

> > Thanks too

messages.subject: Error building rsvg: librsvg-2.0 was not found.
messages.subject_clean: Error building rsvg: librsvg-2.0 was not found.
messages.body_plain:
I think librsvg2 needs to be installed on the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers.  I have an app which requires the following libraries:

library(shiny)
library(devtools)
devtools::install_github('rich-iannone/DiagrammeR')
library(DiagrammeR)

I can run the app locally, but when I try and push it to shinyapps I get the following error.

** package ‘rsvg’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
Package librsvg-2.0 was not found in the pkg-config search path.
Perhaps you should add the directory containing `librsvg-2.0.pc'
to the PKG_CONFIG_PATH environment variable
No package 'librsvg-2.0' found
Using PKG_CFLAGS=
Using PKG_LIBS=-lrsvg
------------------------- ANTICONF ERROR ---------------------------
Configuration failed because librsvg-2.0 was not found. Try installing:
 * deb: librsvg2-dev (Debian, Ubuntu, etc)
 * rpm: librsvg2-devel (Fedora, EPEL)
 * csw: librsvg_dev, sunx11_devel (Solaris)
 * brew: librsvg (OSX)
If librsvg-2.0 is already installed, check that 'pkg-config' is in your
PATH and PKG_CONFIG_PATH contains a librsvg-2.0.pc file. If pkg-config
is unavailable you can set INCLUDE_DIR and LIB_DIR manually via:
R CMD INSTALL --configure-vars='INCLUDE_DIR=... LIB_DIR=...'
--------------------------------------------------------------------
ERROR: configuration failed for package ‘rsvg’
* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/rsvg’
################################### End Log ###################################
Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 176819728 failed: Error building image: Error building rsvg (0.5). Build exited with non-zero status: 1

Note, on my system (Debian) where the app runs I do have librsvg2-dev installed.  Also, if I pull the DiagrammeR package from CRAN (version 0.8.2), which doesn't import the rsvg package, then everything runs fine.  DiagrammeR from GitHub requires the CRAN package rsvg (version 0.5).

Tareef,

Regardless, it seems the build is failing on the CRAN version of rsvg.  To confirm I created a new presentation (see below) with one app which only calls

library(rsvg)

and then plots a random number.  The presentation works on my system with librsvg2-dev installed.  The build on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> again fails on rsvg with the same error message. So it seems shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers don't have the necessary libraries to build rsvg from CRAN.  Is it possible to have the library installed?

Note, the newer version of DiagrammeR on github has important fixes I need.  So I can't use the CRAN version which shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> pulls -- hence the github version.

Thanks for your help.

Matt

---
title: "Example rsvg"
author: ""
affiliation:
date: "03/02/2016"
output: ioslides_presentation
runtime: shiny
smaller: true
---

## Shiny App

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(rsvg)
inputPanel(
   )
renderPlot({
  plot(rnorm(1))
})
```
